name: Stems Per Hectare Calculator
seoTitle: Stems Per Hectare Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: Stem counts for plantations and cane: given the row and stool spacing and the share that survives, how many harvestable stems a hectare will carry. Free stems
summary:
Stem counts for plantations and cane: given the row and stool spacing and the share that survives, how many harvestable stems a hectare will carry. It returns stools per hectare, stems per hectare, stems on the area and stems per square metre, and the panel shows all of them at once.

It is the population that sets the tonnage, so getting it right is the difference between a full cane crop and a thin one. Press Calculate and the results appear in the grey boxes; after the first press they keep up with every edit, so there is no page to reload. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Stems Per Hectare
sections.html:
Stools/ha = 10 000 ÷ (row spacing × stool spacing). Stems/ha = stools/ha × stems per stool × survival

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
stoolthe planted sett and the tillers that grow from it—
survivalshare of stools that establish and overwinter%
stems/haharvestable stalks per hectare/ha

sections.title: How do I use the Stems Per Hectare?
sections.html:
Every input sits in the same order the formula is written, so the page reads like the equation.

  1. Enter the row spacing and the spacing between stools along the row.
  2. Enter how many harvestable stems a stool carries and the survival you expect.
  3. The stool count, stem count and stems per square metre follow.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: area of 1 ha, row spacing of 1.5 m, spacing along the row of 0.5 m, stems per stool of 6, survival of 85%.

Substituting them into the formula gives stools per hectare of 13,333.33 /ha, stems per hectare of 68,000 /ha, stems on the area of 68,000, stems per square metre of 6.8 /m².

Those numbers come from the same solver the page runs in your browser, not from an illustration, so typing different inputs moves the answer exactly as the arithmetic says.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
The number on its own is not a judgement. These are the bands most often used when the result is quoted in a paper, a report or a label:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
under 60 000/haThina poor strike or wide rows; yield will disappoint
60 000 – 120 000/haNormal canea well-established commercial crop
over 150 000/haVery denselodging risk and thinner, lighter stalks

  • Yields scale with stem number up to a point; after that the stalks compete and each one weighs less, so the tonnage levels off.

  • Sugarcane is counted in millable stalks, which excludes the small tillers that never mature — the survival figure should reflect that.

  • For a timber or biomass plantation, the same arithmetic works with stems per hectare as the planted density, before thinning.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
These are the errors that account for almost every wrong answer people bring to this calculator:

  • Counting every tiller as a millable stalk and over-estimating the tonnage by a third.
  • Using the planted spacing without any survival figure, which assumes every sett establishes.
  • Comparing stem counts taken at different ages, before tillering has finished.

Plants per hectare. Crop coefficient. Land equivalent ratio.

faq.q: How many sugarcane stalks per hectare?
faq.a: 60 000–120 000 millable stalks in a commercial crop.

faq.q: How many stools per hectare at 1.5 × 0.5 m?
Does more stems mean more sugar?
faq.a: Up to a point; excessive density lowers stalk weight and increases lodging.

faq.q: What does the Stems Per Hectare actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns stools per hectare, stems per hectare, stems on the area and stems per square metre. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.
